title: Google’s next Genie AI model generates more realistic experiences
slides: Can Google's Genie make game worlds feel real?
The new model generates interactive 3D environments
But realism breaks down on complex physics
Developers can now prototype scenes faster
Test one scene and judge the realism yourself
thread_text:
1. Realism or illusion?

Google's Genie generates interactive 3D worlds from a single image. The demo looks impressive, but early tests show physics glitches when objects collide.

2. From image to world

The model turns any picture into a playable environment. No coding needed—just upload and explore. This could change how games are prototyped.

3. The physics problem

Complex interactions like stacking or fluid dynamics break down. Genie struggles with realistic motion, making some scenes feel off.

4. Prototyping gets faster

Developers can now test scene ideas in minutes instead of days. Speed comes at the cost of accuracy, but it's a start.

5. Try it yourself

Generate a scene with Genie and see if the realism holds up. Would you trust it for your next project? Test one scene today.

instagram.caption:
One image is now enough to generate a playable 3D world, no coding required. 🎮

Google's new Genie model turns any picture into an interactive environment you can explore.

The catch: physics breaks down on complex interactions like stacking objects or fluids. 🧩

Developers can prototype scenes in minutes instead of days, though accuracy still lags behind speed.

If you build games or scenes, you can test a full idea before committing real resources. ⚡

Would you trust a physics-glitchy prototype for your next project, or is realism non-negotiable? 🤔
